source: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 17 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 17
knowledgePattern: Derive a regular tetrahedron radius ratio before summing nested sphere volumes
solution:
Scale a regular tetrahedron to edge length 2. The altitude of a base equilateral triangle is 3, so the distance from its centre to a base vertex is 23/3. By Pythagoras, the tetrahedron’s height is H=4−4/3=4/6.

By the symmetry of the four equal faces, the insphere centre and the circumsphere centre are the same point O on that height. Let t be its distance above the base. Equal distances from O to the top vertex and a base vertex give (H−t)2=t2+4/3. Thus t=1/6. The inner radius is r=t and the outer radius is R=H−t=3/6, so r/R=1/3.

Each new sphere therefore has 1/27 of the previous sphere’s volume. Starting from volume 1, the total is the convergent geometric series 1+1/27+1/272+⋯=1/(1−1/27)=27/26. Answer C.

hints.title: Find a useful right-triangle cross-section
hints.body: Draw the tetrahedron’s height through the centre of an equilateral face. Express the height and the base-centre-to-vertex distance using the common edge length.
hints.recap: A suitable cross-section or projected right triangle reduces a three-dimensional distance problem to two dimensions.
hints.pitfall: A face altitude and the solid’s height are different lengths.
hints.pause: Use the equilateral triangle’s altitude and Pythagoras to obtain the needed distances.

recall.reminder: A suitable cross-section or projected right triangle reduces a three-dimensional distance problem to two dimensions.

hints.title: Locate the common centre by equal distances
hints.body: Use the regular tetrahedron’s symmetry to put its sphere centres on the height. Equate the distances from that centre to a top vertex and a base vertex.
hints.recap: New learning: in a right triangle, the sum of the squared perpendicular sides equals the squared hypotenuse.
hints.pitfall: Do not assume the centre is halfway up the tetrahedron.
hints.pause: Solve for the centre’s height above the face and relate it to both sphere radii.

recall.reminder: New learning: in a right triangle, the sum of the squared perpendicular sides equals the squared hypotenuse.

hints.title: Convert the repeated length ratio into a volume series
hints.body: Once the radius scale is known, apply the corresponding volume scale at each nesting step.
hints.recap: Similar lengths, areas and volumes use the first, second and third powers of the scale factor respectively.
hints.pitfall: A radius ratio is not a volume ratio.
hints.pause: Identify the first term and common ratio, check convergence and sum every sphere starting with the original.

recall.reminder: Similar lengths, areas and volumes use the first, second and third powers of the scale factor respectively.
